issues.should_be: The email states 'Coming back from a friend's birthday party, where I had a few drinks, I lost control and hit a fence' — an admission of alcohol consumption before driving, which is a possible exclusion signal under contract Article 3.1 ('the driver had alcohol above the legal limit'); the handler should have flagged it instead of recording null
issues.evidence: Customer email 'where I had a few drinks'; contract Article 3.1 alcohol exclusion and 'When a claim shows a possible exclusion, it is referred to a claims handler' <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>

Deadline is fine (reported 2026-10-22, one day after the 2026-10-21 incident, within the 5 days of Article 4.1 <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>), coverage C2 is in the Policy Schedule, and the required C2 documents (photos, repair quote) were provided, so none of those block payment. The handler-playbook rule about commercial vehicles does not apply because the email states no third party was involved. However, the email states the driver 'had a few drinks' before driving, which is a possible exclusion under contract Article 3.1 (alcohol); Article 3 and Article 7.2 require that a claim showing a possible exclusion be referred to a Veridia claims handler who takes the decision — it must not be paid automatically. The staged automatic payout (pending_approval, €1500) should therefore not be approved as-is; the claim must go to a handler because of the unrecorded possible alcohol exclusion.
